findings.summary: The regressions do not prove that blocking lifecycle startup remains off the event-loop thread.
findings.diagnosis: The repair's contract is a lifecycle-dedicated executor, but the ContextVar test only observes propagated values and the starvation test only proves that startup is not queued behind the saturated default executor. Replacing run_in_executor with a direct context.run(_install_and_startup, ...) call on the event-loop thread preserves the ContextVar values, sets lifecycle_started, avoids the shared-pool deadlock, and leaves every changed assertion green while reintroducing event-loop blocking.
findings.evidence: The callbacks at lines 116-126 record only ContextVar values, and observed_initialize_di at lines 185-187 records only that startup began. Neither compares the callback thread with the calling event-loop thread or the dedicated lifecycle executor.
findings.correction: Record the event-loop thread identity before initialization and assert that initialize_di and the cache startup callback execute on a different thread, alongside the existing exact-identity ContextVar assertions. Retain a red counterfactual that invokes lifecycle work directly on the event-loop thread.
